newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scitex cautiously optimistic on future.
newsitem.headline: Scitex cautiously optimistic on future.

text.p: Scitex Corp management's outlook is one of "cautious optimism" following the release of better-than-expected second quarter results, president and chief executive Yoav Chelouche said on Tuesday.

Scitex on Monday reported a net profit of $157,000 in the second quarter. This follows several quarters of sharp losses which had prompted Scitex to undertake a massive restructuring of its graphic arts business.
Analysts such as Lehman Brothers' Ted Kundtz had expected Scitex to post a loss of $0.14 a share in the second quarter, similar to the year ago loss.
Chelouche declined to give a forecast for the coming quarters but hinted at continued improvement.
"We are closing a quarter which can definitely be seen as a good one. The mood we are projecting is cautious optimism," he told Reuters.
"The strongest quarter in the year is typically the fourth quarter," he added.
While the company is further along than expected in implementing the graphic arts group's restructuring, Chelouche said there was plenty of work ahead.
"This is indeed a good milestone on our way, having reached the break-even point and a positive cash flow. But it is not the end of the road," he said.
Once the flagship of Israel's high-tech sector, the maker of electronic prepress, digitial printing and digital video systems has seen its share price fall from $44 in 1992 to below $7 in April.
The shares have since recovered slightly. They climbed 1.7 percent to 11-5/16 on Monday after earnings were announced.
Chelouche attributed the results to an emphasis on costs, operating efficiency and product quality improvement.
Chief financial officer Eyal Desheh said the results were just slightly better than the company's internal plan.
"Our forecast was somewhat better than what analysts had said," he said.
Despite improved operating results, revenues in the second quarter slipped to $167 million from $190 million in the year ago quarter but rose from $163 million in the first quarter.
Desheh said it was difficult to make comparisons with 1996.

"As compared to a year ago Scitex is a different company. Revenues are down but they represent more profit. We are concentrating on better quality of business. We only sell what we can make a profit from," he said.
Graphic arts revenues totalled $114 million against $135 million in the year earlier quarter and up two percent from the first quarter of 1997.

The digital printing group's revenues were $38 million against $40 million a year earlier. But company officials noted that last year's figure included a one-time sale of $6 million to Nippon Telephone & Telegraph.
The results of its digital video group were below plan. Revenues were $16 million, up from $15 million in last year's weak second quarter and down 12 percent from the first quarter of 1997.
"We are as a management team giving video a very close treatment," said Desheh.
He said the group had completed a new line of products later than anticipated.
"Clients require upgrades in software and additional features the company had promised and did not deliver on time," he said.

The group is implementing a recovery plan, which on the product side includes the completion of the Sphere line of editing work stations. On the operating side the plan calls for cost containments but no sackings.
"The third quarter (for the video group) won't be much stronger than this one and if so only marginally," Desheh said.
"We don't expect a turnaround before the fourth quarter of the year. It is not something that will happen overnight but we believe it can be done," Desheh said.
